key: e:university of pretoria vehicle dynamics group
synopsis: The University of Pretoria Vehicle Dynamics Group acts as the independent verifier for the South African mining industry's MOSH regime and has worked with mining organizations and an ISO working group [f15795, f1357, f15799]. Its methodology, described in 2020, progresses from controlled laboratory tests to interaction tests in a representative mine, using high-precision GPS as surface ground truth and combinations of lidar, cameras and automotive radar underground; it opened an underground test facility in December 2020 [f1355, f15796, f1356, f1358, f15798]. Across 189 tests, it reported pass rates of 62 percent for detection devices, 42 percent for machine-side systems and 83 percent for third-party interfaces, alongside a testing rate of 1.6 tests per week and an 18-week lead time [f15800, f15801]. The corpus identifies these as the only published independent results for automatic slow-down and stop in mining, limiting the available independent evidence base [f15802]. Its 2024 research found that conservative collision-avoidance systems suffer false-positive interventions causing production losses, increased wear and resistance to adoption, and investigated adding steering rate to collision prediction using modeled South African mining scenarios [f15803, f15804].

relations.note: Both describe the 2020 progression from laboratory testing to representative-mine interaction tests.
Both date the underground test facility opening to December 2020.
Both report collaboration with mining organizations and an ISO working group.
Specifies surface and underground ground-truth instruments used in the verification methodology.
Describes the testing methodology underlying the group's independent-verifier role.
Quantifies the published independent results by test count and subsystem pass rates.
Adds reported testing throughput and lead time to the staged testing methodology.
Adds collision-prediction variables and scenario-modeling methods investigated in the same 2024 research.
